# `⊂` — Enclose / Partitioned enclose

`⊂Y` makes a rank-zero array containing `Y`.

[Parentheses](parentheses.qmd) round a literal also make a scalar: `(1 2)` is `⊂1 2`. [Brackets](brackets.qmd) round one item make a one-item vector, not a scalar. `⊂` cannot enclose a function, because `⊂` next to a function forms a train. Parentheses round a glyph enclose it instead: `(+)` is a scalar holding `+`. Parentheses round a name only group, so a named function has no enclosing spelling of its own: `⍬⍴[f]` reshapes a one-item vector to a scalar.

```apl
⍴⊂1 2 3            ⍝ 0⍴0ₓ
↑⊂1 2 3            ⍝ 1 2 3
(⊂3)≡3             ⍝ 0ₓ
(1 2)≡⊂1 2          ⍝ 1
```

With [axes](axis.qmd), `⊂⍠K Y` encloses cells on axes `K`.

```apl
⊂⍠1 (2 3⍴⍳6)       ⍝ [[0 1 2] [3 4 5]]
```

`N⊂Y` starts partitions at positive marks along the leading axis. Each partition is a block of major cells. Leading zero marks are ignored.

```apl
1 0 1 0⊂"abcd"     ⍝ "ab" "cd"
1 0 1⊂3 2⍴⍳6       ⍝ [[0 1 ⋄ 2 3] [4 5 ⋄]]
```

A mark greater than 1 starts extra empty partitions. Unit marks extend. `N⊂⍠K Y` partitions along axis `K` instead. `N⊂⍤1 Y` partitions each row.

```apl
1 0 1⊂⍠1 (2 3⍴⍳6)  ⍝ [[0 1 ⋄ 3 4] [[2] ⋄ [5]]]
1 0 1⊂⍤1 (2 3⍴⍳6)  ⍝ [[0 1] [2] ⋄ [3 4] [5]]
```

See also [`⊆`](nest.qmd).
